cohort: The study included labor and delivery admissions from the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2020), categorized into three cohorts: prior bariatric surgery (22,685 cases), obesity without prior bariatric surgery (2.1 million controls), and controls without obesity (16.37 million).
finding: Pregnancy after bariatric surgery is associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery and postpartum complications relative to the general population with obesity, but may have higher rates of some adverse outcomes like cesarean delivery and breech presentation when compared to controls without obesity.
mod_finding: Compared to controls with obesity, the bariatric surgery cohort had lower rates of cesarean delivery (aOR 0.72), while compared to controls without obesity, the bariatric surgery group had higher rates of cesarean delivery (aOR 1.43) and lower rates of assisted delivery (aOR 0.54).
